Lemma: H4120

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "Quickly, speedily, in haste — an adverb urging swift action or describing rapid occurrence"
  Readable gloss: "An adverbial noun from the root מהר ('to hasten') used throughout the Hebrew Bible to express urgency and speed. It often follows a verb to intensify the rapidity of action — Aaron must go quickly to make atonement and stop the plague (Num 16:46), the Gibeonites plead 'come up to us quickly and save us' (Josh 10:6), and Hushai warns David to cross the Jordan quickly lest he be swallowed up (2 Sam 17:16). In poetic texts it precedes the verb for emphasis: Isaiah pictures God summoning a distant nation that comes swiftly (Isa 5:26), and the psalmist prays 'be a rock of refuge to me; hasten to deliver me' (Ps 31:3)."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "quickly, speedily, swiftly"
    Enriched: The adverb מְהֵרָה (meherah), 'quickly, speedily, in haste,' expressing urgency or swiftness of action. Typically follows the verb in prose (Josh 8:19, the ambush rises quickly; 2 Sam 17:16, 21, David must flee quickly) and precedes it in poetry for heightened effect (Isa 5:26; Ps 31:3). Spanish renders variously as 'apresuradamente/pronto/prisa,' German sometimes leaves the Hebrew untransliterate...
    Existing Spanish translations: apresuradamente, prisa, pronto, rápidamente, rápido
